external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A person who browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party payment processor that settles payments and sends payment webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service on Cloud Run through which shoppers browse and place orders, and which receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker in the core network that processes orders, reads and writes the orders database, and writes completed-order receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Shopper sign-in to the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: Shopper browsing and order placement through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: call order service
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC

data_flows.name: read-write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values in the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for each completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket
data_flows.data_description: Receipt recording which order was written and that the order service wrote it

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor sends a webhook to the storefront API after settling a payment.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API
data_flows.notes: The source says: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."
data_flows.data_description: Payment-settlement notification identifying that an order is paid

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The core network in which the order service runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: card processor
trust_boundaries.description: The third-party environment controlled by the card processor.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The orders database contents are confidential because they include shopper addresses and card-last-four values.
assumptions.basis: The source states that orders-db contains shopper addresses and card-last-four values, which are personal and payment-related data.
